canonical_data: local working trees and Git worktrees, .devin rules, skills, workflows, and plans, legacy Cascade memories under the user's home directory, and service-side accounts, usage, and optional remote repository indexes
current_repo_note: Renamed from Windsurf on 2026-06-02 following Cognition's July 2025 acquisition of the product, IP, trademark, and brand from Exafunction; the vendor states that only the name and branding changed, so this is one record under the rename rule rather than a supersession. windsurf.com and codeium.com now redirect to the Devin Desktop product page, while legacy Windsurf plan settings, the team admin portal, the remote-indexing console, and the Windsurf editor plugins keep the Windsurf name. The record is distinct from the published Devin record, which is the cloud agent Cognition sells as a separate SKU.
strengths: An Agent Client Protocol host: any conforming third-party agent — Codex, Claude Agent, OpenCode, Junie, Gemini CLI — becomes a first-class session inside the editor

The default local agent carries a permission model with deny, ask, and allow rules over file reads, writes, command execution, HTTP fetches, and MCP tools, scoped at project, user, and organization level
The widest reviewed provider surface among proprietary editors, spanning nine model families alongside an in-house model line and a purpose-built retrieval model
weaknesses: Two local agents ship side by side with divergent controls, and the pages a reader lands on for memories, MCP, and command auto-execution are all scoped to the legacy one
Durable memory does not survive adopting the default agent, which does not persist memories at all and offers a migration wizard instead
The announced end of the legacy agent has passed without resolution: the vendor said it remained available through July, and it is still documented and still appearing in the August changelog

Customer data may be used for model training by default, the opt-out is available only on paid plans and only to administrators on team plans, and remote indexing clones repositories to vendor servers
Third-party agents hosted over the protocol run outside the product's own governance — the vendor states its privacy policy and legal terms do not apply to them
why_it_matters: The rename that consolidated the best-known independent agentic IDE into Cognition's line, and the reviewed catalog's clearest case of an editor that hosts other vendors' agents as peers rather than replacing them.
